鬼滅の刃 [Kimetsu no Yaiba] #22

Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba, Vol. 22

Koyoharu Gotouge

4.69
16,946 ratings825 reviews
Rate this book
In Taisho-era Japan, kindhearted Tanjiro Kamado makes a living selling charcoal. But his peaceful life is shattered when a demon slaughters his entire family. His little sister Nezuko is the only survivor, but she has been transformed into a demon herself! Tanjiro sets out on a dangerous journey to find a way to return his sister to normal and destroy the demon who ruined his life.

After centuries of preparation and training, the Demon Slayer Corps has come face-to-face with their nemesis, Muzan Kibutsuji. It is a desperate battle and several Demon Slayers have already been killed. Tanjiro himself has engaged Muzan, and, despite giving it everything he has, is taken out of the fight! Although severely injured and near death, he sees a vision of his ancestor that may hold the key to finally destroying Muzan! Can Tanjiro recover enough strength to fight Muzan to the finish?

February 9, 2026
If those things we call demons didn't exist in this world, I have no idea how many people would still be alive now. If you and I met under more peaceful and carefree circumstances, I wonder how well things would've gone. [Obanai]

With Demon Slayer's Volume 22 we continue the final battle against Muzan. With Tanjiro down, all the living Hashiras are doing their best to endure until dawn, but despite their combined strengths, Muzan's merciless wide-ranged attacks make them feel overwhelmed and helpless, and reduce their movements to just dodging by pure instincts alone. The situation looks incredibly bad, and gets even worse when the Hashiras power suddenly decreases through one of them being struck down.

If we reincarnate as human beings into a world without demons, then I will definitely tell you that I love you. [Obanai]

I can't say that I ever was an Obanai x Mitsuri shipper. I heard about them being a popular ship, but I never paid much attention, more interested in other characters. I also wasn't very curious about Obanai's past, he never ranked high in a list of my favorite Hashiras.

Demon Slayer's Volume 22 changed that.

I never thought that my Hashiras ranking would ever change, but because of this volume, Obanai got a huge promotion. Sanemi's, Giyuu's and Tengen's positions will never change, but Obanai secured himself a spot in the Top 5, easily (to clear things up: the fourth place belongs to Mitsuri). I am in love with him as an individual character and with him and Mitsuri as a pairing. They are so cute together, how I have never seen it before is truly beyond me! She is his sunshine and he is her strength, I believe in it wholeheartedly and I will go down with this ship. I wonder how long they liked each other romantically and I'm drowning in sorrow whenever I think about them, because they never made a confession about their feelings for each other.

"You're a sacrifice! You should have stayed quiet and let her eat you!" [Obanai's nameless cousin]

All of Hashiras backstories (except for Mitsuri's) were tough to get through considering all the trauma, pain and loss, and Obanai's one wasn't any different (I never thought that I would cry over Obanai of all people). It was shocking, incredibly shocking to be honest, maybe not because of the presence of the demon and its impact on the story, but mostly because of the human cruelty. We all know the nature of the demons, we expect them to be merciless, but the humans acting with an absolute cruelty, especially towards their own children, was something completely unexpected. I mean, it's not like Demon Slayer's humans are just constant victims, no, I just want to point out how painful it is to see such a cruelty shown by humans who should stick together against the danger of the demons instead of working alongside them and sacrificing other lives, their own children's lives, for the demon's sake.

And the fact that Obanai's cousin blamed him for the deaths of their family members, more content to see hi, get eaten, than their family members pay for all the years of their cruelty, was something truly bizarre. I couldn't believe what I was seeing. She cried because of their family fates, but blamed her cousin (who was completely innocent), because he dared to escape his death sentence. What a freaking hypocrite. She lived a peaceful life, in love and luxury, happy and content, despite knowing what was happening in the shadows of their household for years, never facing the obstacles that Obanai (and other children, I assume) had to face. She was never supposed to be a sacrifice, so it was fine. Who cared about the children who were never this lucky? They were lives that could've been easily sacrificed, nothing more nothing less. It's terrifying that a human could do such a thing to another human, especially in a universe plagued by demons.

P.S. God bless Kaburamaru's existence 🥺

"Don't struggle in vain! Just die like men, you obsessed freaks!" [Muzan]

Remember how intimidated I felt of Muzan's presence while reading the previous volume? I was always making fun of him, but back then his villain aura was unmatched. The situation looked so hopeless that I wanted to cry and beg for help. It still felt this way during Volume 22, for a little while at least. But suddenly the situation had changed, and when Muzan decided to run for his life, I started to laugh and I couldn't stop for a long time.

"Of course! Muzan isn't a samurai with pride or a human being who acts on emotion. He's a thing that only clings to life!" [Obanai]

Muzan acted so high and mighty, comparing himself to the unstoppable force of nature that you cannot fight against, only begging for it to be merciful. He laughed at the Hashiras faces, mocking them for trying to cut him down, harming them over and over again, confident that none of them is a threat and completely missing the obvious signs that something was wrong. Did he seriously think that Tamayo and Shinobu, two of the strongest women in Demon Slayer, would go down without any further plan? That their deaths mean that they cannot harm him anymore?

What a funny guy!

He escaped from certain death by Yoriichi's hands and he thought he could do the same stunt now. But not on Tanjiro's watch, my guy. Not on Tanjiro's watch.

"You look positively awful, Tanjiro Kamado. This way it's hard to tell which one of us is the demon." [Muzan]

Tanjiro was always tactical, clever and strong, surviving things that other people wouldn't. After losing his family and after Nezuko's transformation to a demon, he could have easily lost himself in grief and madness, but he never stopped fighting for Nezuko, for his friends, and for himself. He stood up and faced his opponents, one after another, over and over again, no matter what injuries he had to endure. Despite it all, he never lost his kind nature, slaying the demons, but staying with them and offering them warmth and comfort in their last journey.

Seeing him now, so injured, so raw and ready for his final battle against his family's killer, was so incredibly impressive that I jumped out of my seat and cheered. I thought that Muzan's aura from the previous volume was unmatched, but it was nothing in comparison to a single image of Tanjiro facing Muzan from Volume 22. Dear author, thank you for it. Thank you from the bottom of my heart.

"Don't let him get away!! We can stop him together!!" [Tanjiro]

As much as the image of the Hashiras being down pains me, I can't help, but feel happy, because we got an opportunity to see Tanjiro and Obanai team up. I always loved Tanjiro with Giyuu, and I would love to see them fighting side by side again, but the Tanjiro and Obanai duo is a beautiful surprise, I cannot be mad about it. Obanai's snake breathing is amazing, and Tanjiro's strikes match it perfectly, I like it a lot and I hope to see more of it!

There is only one volume left to the end! I can't believe that I'm so close to finishing this amazing series!

P.S. Yushiro, Tamayo and Shinobu are the absolute MVPS of this arc. I am so happy to see it. Yushiro's so clever with using his invisibility and Tamayo and Shinobu haunting Muzan even beyond the grave is outstanding. They are getting their revenge, hopefully Muzan dies while suffering (I will riot if this will not happen).

A ver, como final de manga, lo que he leído en este volumen me ha gustado a grandes rasgos. La pelea final contra Muzan está siendo de lo más intensa con cada capitulo. La adrenalina corre a borbotones al ritmo de giros inesperados y situaciones de vida y muerte, y me tiene completamente enganchada, cada vez que vuelvo a coger “Kimetsu no Yaiba”acabo con el alma en vilo. Sé que me repito mucho, pero si hay algo que valoro mucho de esta historia es lo humana y realista que es, como sus personajes casi agonizan en cada combate al ser heridos, como sus pasados condicionan su forma de ser.

Pero como final general de manga, todo le está pareciendo demasiado apresurado. Es cierto que los últimos capítulos, y concretamente en este tomo, se están empezando a cerrar muchas de las cuestiones que aún estaban en el aire. Pero aún noto que a un solo volumen de finiquitar la historia queda muchos asuntos que no están cerrados del todo. Cada capítulo que he leído me ha parecido demasiado frenético como para poder disfrutarlo realmente. Entiendo que en un tomo tan enfocado en la acción bélica esto sea normal. Pero al estar en la recta final del manga esto se me queda en muy poco. Echo en falta más argumento que el mero combate.

No obstante, insisto: me está gustando lo que leo. Gotouge-sensei está manejando muy bien la intensidad que este volumen desprende por los cuatro costados. No hay ni un momento de respiro, todo el rato están pasando cosas. Y además, la autora ha vuelto a acordarse de personajes que llevaba varios capítulos teniendo olvidados y ha empezado a aprovecharlos, algo que personalmente lo agradezco mucho.


Y con todo esto… solo me queda un volumen😭. A ver cómo termina la cosa. Me da pena acabar ya este manga.

Wow, the desperation and determination displayed in this volume was insane! No joke, I could feel the desperation and anxiety the Hashira and the others were feeling during this fight. Watching everyone struggle to keep Muzan occupied until dawn was interesting because it reminded me of that phrase, "throwing things at a wall until something sticks". Everyone is trying every tactic, every technique, trying to find any advantage to prolong the fight and I could feel their desperation, exhaustion, hopelessness, and determination. Because even when things kept getting worse, they never gave up; they just tried something, anything to keep moving. And I fucking love that.

Iguro got to be center stage this volume and while it's sad that his backstory wasn't given until now (you know, ONE VOLUME BEFORE THE SERIES ENDS), it was truly haunting and fit the theme of family either being an inspiration or a curse. And HOLY SHIT, was Iguro's family a curse! That scene with him and the snake demon made me nearly throw up. It also makes sense why he loves Kanroji so much (not that you need a reason, she's amazing) but it was sweet seeing him try to protect her as best he can. Also, him teaming up with Tanjiro near the end was great.

But most importantly of all, Tamayo and Shinobu are officially the MVPs of this fight because those ladies fucked up Muzan before the real fight even started! Seriously, I don't care what anyone says, NONE of the Hashira OR Tanjiro would be able to stand to Muzan if Tamayo and Shinobu hadn't created the toxic concoction for him. They deserve all the credit for making this fight possible from the start and I love them both!

That's all I've got for now. One more volume, the end is near!
